questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Heparin acts by:
options: Activating antithrombin III, which then inactivates thrombin and factor Xa
questions.concept: Unfractionated heparin acts immediately and is monitored by APTT, with protamine sulphate as antidote. Low molecular weight heparins act mainly on factor Xa, need no monitoring and are only partly reversed by protamine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Warfarin has a delayed onset of action because:
options: Existing clotting factors must be cleared, with factor II having the longest half-life
questions.concept: Warfarin blocks synthesis of new factors II, VII, IX and X, so heparin cover is needed for the first days. Paradoxical early hypercoagulability from rapid loss of protein C causes warfarin-induced skin necrosis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Warfarin is contraindicated in pregnancy because it causes:
options: Fetal warfarin syndrome with nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses, and fetal haemorrhage
questions.concept: Warfarin crosses the placenta and is teratogenic in the first trimester and causes fetal intracranial haemorrhage near term, so heparin, which does not cross the placenta, is used instead.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Clopidogrel exerts its antiplatelet effect by:
options: Irreversibly blocking the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor
questions.concept: Clopidogrel is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation, so poor metabolisers and concurrent omeprazole reduce efficacy. Prasugrel and ticagrelor are alternatives with more consistent effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: The principal risk of thrombolytic therapy with streptokinase or alteplase is:
questions.concept: Absolute contraindications include previous intracranial haemorrhage, ischaemic stroke within 3 months, active bleeding, aortic dissection and recent major surgery. Streptokinase is antigenic and cannot be repeated within a year.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Direct oral anticoagulants such as rivaroxaban and dabigatran are preferred over warfarin because they:
options: Need no routine monitoring and have fewer food and drug interactions
questions.concept: They are contraindicated in mechanical heart valves and severe renal impairment. Idarucizumab reverses dabigatran and andexanet alfa reverses factor Xa inhibitors.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Statins lower cholesterol principally by:
options: Inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase and upregulating hepatic LDL receptors
questions.concept: Reduced intracellular cholesterol increases LDL receptor expression, clearing LDL from plasma. Statins also have pleiotropic plaque-stabilising and anti-inflammatory effects, and are best taken at night.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Ezetimibe lowers cholesterol by:
options: Inhibiting the NPC1L1 transporter blocking intestinal cholesterol absorption
questions.concept: It gives an additional 15 to 20% LDL reduction when added to a statin, useful when statin dose is limited by myopathy. PCSK9 inhibitors give far greater reductions by preventing LDL receptor degradation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Fibrates act mainly on triglycerides by:
options: Activating PPAR-alpha, increasing lipoprotein lipase activity
questions.concept: Fenofibrate and gemfibrozil are first line for severe hypertriglyceridaemia to prevent pancreatitis. Combination with statins increases myopathy risk, particularly with gemfibrozil.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics & hypolipidaemics
questions.stem: Aspirin and clopidogrel dual therapy is typically given after:
options: Coronary stent placement, to prevent stent thrombosis
questions.concept: Dual antiplatelet therapy prevents stent thrombosis while endothelialisation occurs, with duration depending on stent type and bleeding risk. Atrial fibrillation instead requires anticoagulation, not antiplatelet therapy.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Combined oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy principally by:
options: Suppressing the LH surge and thereby inhibiting ovulation
questions.concept: Negative feedback on gonadotrophin release prevents ovulation, with secondary effects of thickened cervical mucus and an unfavourable endometrium. Failure rate is under 1% with perfect use.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Combined oral contraceptives are absolutely contraindicated in:
options: A woman over 35 who smokes heavily, or with a history of thromboembolism
questions.concept: The oestrogen component increases thrombotic risk, compounded by smoking after 35, migraine with aura, known thrombophilia and oestrogen-dependent tumours. Progestogen-only methods are safer alternatives.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Levonorgestrel emergency contraception is most effective when taken:
options: As soon as possible and within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse
questions.concept: Efficacy declines with delay. Ulipristal is effective up to 120 hours, and the copper intrauterine device inserted within 5 days is the most effective emergency method and provides ongoing contraception.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Mifepristone is used in medical abortion because it:
options: Antagonises progesterone receptors, sensitising the myometrium to prostaglandins
questions.concept: Mifepristone followed 24 to 48 hours later by misoprostol achieves complete abortion in over 95% of early pregnancies, and is permitted under the MTP Act up to 9 weeks by a registered practitioner.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Oxytocin differs from ergometrine in that oxytocin:
options: Produces rhythmic contractions with relaxation between, so it can be used before delivery of the fetus
questions.concept: Ergometrine causes sustained tonic contraction and is only used after delivery, and is contraindicated in hypertension and pre-eclampsia. Oxytocin has antidiuretic action, risking water intoxication in high-dose infusions.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Tamoxifen acts as a selective oestrogen receptor modulator that is:
options: Antagonist in the breast but agonist in the endometrium and bone
questions.concept: This tissue selectivity gives benefit in ER-positive breast cancer and preserves bone density but increases endometrial carcinoma and thromboembolic risk, so abnormal bleeding must always be investigated.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Bisphosphonates must be taken:
options: Fasting with a full glass of water, remaining upright for 30 minutes
questions.concept: Poor oral bioavailability requires fasting administration, and staying upright prevents oesophagitis and ulceration. Absorption is abolished by calcium, iron and antacids taken simultaneously.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Teriparatide, recombinant parathyroid hormone, increases bone mass because:
options: Intermittent administration stimulates osteoblasts, unlike continuous PTH excess which causes resorption
questions.concept: Teriparatide is the principal anabolic agent for severe osteoporosis, used for a limited period because of osteosarcoma concerns in animal studies, and followed by an antiresorptive to maintain the gain.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Finasteride is contraindicated in women of childbearing potential because it:
questions.concept: Even handling crushed tablets is discouraged in pregnancy. In men it treats benign prostatic hyperplasia and androgenetic alopecia, and lowers PSA by about half, which must be accounted for in cancer screening.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Sex hormones, contraceptives, uterine & bone drugs
questions.stem: Danazol acts in endometriosis by:
options: Producing a hypo-oestrogenic hyperandrogenic state suppressing gonadotrophins
questions.concept: Its androgenic side effects - hirsutism, acne, voice deepening and weight gain - limit use, so combined pills, progestogens, dienogest and GnRH analogues with add-back therapy are generally preferred.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Levodopa is combined with carbidopa in order to:
options: Inhibit peripheral dopa decarboxylase, increasing brain delivery and reducing nausea
questions.concept: Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so it blocks only peripheral conversion, allowing the levodopa dose to be reduced by about 75% with far less nausea, hypotension and arrhythmia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Pyridoxine reduces the effect of levodopa when given without carbidopa because it:
options: Is a cofactor for peripheral dopa decarboxylase, increasing peripheral conversion
questions.concept: Vitamin B6 accelerates peripheral metabolism leaving less levodopa for the brain. With a decarboxylase inhibitor this interaction is largely abolished, so modern combinations are unaffected.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: The on-off phenomenon in long-term levodopa therapy refers to:
options: Abrupt unpredictable fluctuations between mobility and immobility
questions.concept: Progressive loss of dopaminergic terminals narrows the therapeutic window. Management includes more frequent smaller doses, COMT and MAO-B inhibitors, dopamine agonists and eventually deep brain stimulation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Anticholinergics such as trihexyphenidyl are most useful in Parkinsonism for:
options: Tremor, particularly in younger patients and drug-induced parkinsonism
questions.concept: They restore the dopamine-acetylcholine balance in the striatum and are the treatment of choice for drug-induced parkinsonism, where levodopa would be ineffective. They are avoided in the elderly because of confusion.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Selegiline acts by:
options: Selectively inhibiting MAO-B, reducing central dopamine breakdown
questions.concept: MAO-B selectivity avoids the cheese reaction of non-selective MAO inhibitors at usual doses. Entacapone instead inhibits COMT, prolonging levodopa action and reducing end-of-dose wearing off.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Baclofen relieves spasticity by acting as:
options: A GABA-B receptor agonist in the spinal cord
questions.concept: Baclofen reduces spasticity in multiple sclerosis and spinal injury, and may be given intrathecally for severe cases. Abrupt withdrawal, especially of intrathecal therapy, causes seizures and rebound spasticity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Dantrolene acts peripherally by:
options: Blocking calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum via the ryanodine receptor
questions.concept: This direct muscle action makes dantrolene the specific antidote for malignant hyperthermia and useful in neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Hepatotoxicity limits long-term oral use for spasticity.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Botulinum toxin relieves focal spasticity and dystonia by:
options: Preventing acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
questions.concept: Cleavage of SNARE proteins gives chemical denervation lasting about 3 months until new terminals sprout. It is used for cervical dystonia, blepharospasm, spasticity, achalasia, hyperhidrosis and cosmetically.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Dopamine agonists such as pramipexole may be preferred as initial therapy in young patients because they:
options: Delay the onset of levodopa-induced dyskinesias
questions.concept: They are less potent than levodopa but delay motor complications in younger patients with a long disease course ahead. Impulse control disorders such as pathological gambling are a distinctive adverse effect.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle relaxants & drugs for Parkinsonism
questions.stem: Amantadine is useful in Parkinsonism because it:
options: Enhances dopamine release and blocks NMDA receptors, reducing dyskinesia
questions.concept: Amantadine gives modest symptomatic benefit and is particularly valued for reducing levodopa-induced dyskinesia. It causes livedo reticularis and ankle oedema, and was originally an antiviral against influenza A.
